findings: All 11 source calibration artifact hashes were independently recomputed and match the immutable authorization subject; its embedded canonical subject digest also recomputes exactly.
The raw 15-rps one-GPU evidence establishes overload without a catastrophic backlog: 14.4 completions/s, queue depth 15 to 21, and +0.582 requests/s persistent positive drift.

The raw 20-rps two-GPU evidence establishes usable drain capacity: 19.9 completions/s with balanced measurement completions, bounded queue behavior, and approximately 5 rps nominal headroom above the unchanged 15-rps offered stream.

The authorization methodology correctly keeps one global offered stream at exactly 15 rps after GPU1 joins and requires observed aggregate completed service greater than offered load; it does not require the system to reproduce the 20-rps calibration rate.

The queue-drain gate is appropriately fail-closed: a trigger backlog in the declared 10-to-25-request range must materially drain with sustained negative slope, and restore cannot begin until a complete five-second SLO-stability window passes.
This approval binds only the immutable authorization subject and its source evidence; live load-generator/controller conformance remains an independent pre-GPU implementation gate.

Required before launch: the live trigger must honor the fixed 20-request trigger inside the preferred 10-to-25 range using the already-approved overload evidence.
